visual.general_description: Scanned histopathology report page with headings for clinical history, macroscopy, microscopy and special stains.
visual.detailed_description: A scanned page titled HISTOPATHOLOGY. Sections are headed CLINICAL HISTORY, MACROSCOPY, MICROSCOPY and Special stains. The clinical history line describes a 4 year old male with cirrhosis of the liver seen macroscopically and a history of haemangioma of the left lobe; biopsies from the left and right lobe are stated as submitted. Macroscopy lists a left lobe wedge and a right lobe wedge with millimetre dimensions. Microscopy text says both specimens look similar, with marked distortion of normal architecture, regenerative-type nodules and fibrosis, some dilatation of veins in the areas of fibrosis, no definitive haemangioma, mild duct proliferation, focal vessel dilatation and mild patchy chronic inflammation in the fibrous septa, no evidence of malignancy, no definitive evidence of alpha anti-trypsin disease, Wilson's disease, viral hepatitis or an obstructive pattern, and no definitive bile duct malformation. Five special stains are listed: Masson Trichrome, Reticulin, Perl's Prussian Blue, PAS/DPAS and Corcein, each with a one-line result. A boxed row of administrative tick options (File, Phone patient, Make appointment, Prescribe, Draw file) and the start of a page footer lie at the bottom.

visual.general_description: Scanned histopathology comment and diagnosis page.
visual.detailed_description: A scanned page with a bold COMMENT section followed by an ICD 10 coding line and a shaded DIAGNOSIS box. The comment says the morphology is that of an established inactive micronodular-type cirrhosis with no overt aetiological agent identified, discusses congenital hepatic fibrosis as a differential that cannot be confirmed on a subcapsular wedge biopsy, recommends looking for stigmata of polycystic kidney disease, states there is no evidence of overt cholangitis, records that the case was reviewed within the laboratory by two named colleagues with a consensus of inactive established micronodular-type cirrhosis, recommends excluding polycystic renal disease and metabolic causes such as alpha 1 anti-trypsin deficiency and Wilson's disease, and says that pending this the case is best regarded as cryptogenic cirrhosis at present. It adds that discussion with paediatricians and the referring clinicians suggests "no hepatitic picture" and no gross abnormality of liver function. The DIAGNOSIS box lists, for left and right liver lobes, "ESTABLISHED MICRONODULAR-TYPE CIRRHOSIS" and "NO OBVIOUS AETIOLOGICAL AGENT".

visual.general_description: Scanned cardiology report page with a measurement table, history and examination text, and the start of the echocardiography findings.
visual.detailed_description: A scanned, slightly noisy page. At the top is a three-column measurement table with headings 2D, M-Mode and Doppler. Under 2D are rows Ao Diam, IVC, LPA, MPA, RPA and a second Ao Diam with values in mm. Under M-Mode are IVSd, LVIDd, LVPWd, LVIDs, EF(Teich), %FS, Ao Diam, LA Diam and LA/Ao. Under Doppler are TR Vmax and TR maxPG. Below is a heading History & Examination with a paragraph from a cardiologist replying to a referring doctor: a boy from Botswana, with abdominal distension since early infancy by the mother's report, hepatic haemangiomata diagnosed in infancy and treated with propranolol, now referred for surgical resection, a laparotomy on a printed calendar date with a cirrhotic liver and no resectable mass, cyanosis and digital clubbing, suspected pulmonary arteriovenous malformations, then examination findings (no dysmorphism, deep cyanosis with a saturation on nasal oxygen, marked digital clubbing, plethoric conjunctivae, no oedema, jaundice or ascites, a pulse rate, no cardiomegaly, normal heart sounds with a 2/6 ejection systolic murmur, no gallop, abdominal distension, hepatomegaly and splenomegaly of stated size, and "??Portal hypertension"). The heading Echocardiography follows with line items for ECG rhythm, cardiac position, systemic veins, atrium and atrial septum, interventricular septum and atrioventricular valves, all described as normal.

visual.general_description: Scanned continuation of the cardiology report with remaining echocardiography findings, diagnosis and recommendations.
visual.detailed_description: A scanned, noisy page with echocardiography line items for ventricles, semilunar valves, great vessels, pericardium and a Miscellaneous entry describing a contrast echo with agitated saline injected into a central venous line, microbubbles arriving in the right atrium and right ventricle and returning to the left atrium and ventricle after a few cardiac cycles, called a positive bubble test confirming pulmonary arteriovenous malformations. A Diagnosis list follows, then Recommendations (counselling of the mother, an accepted saturation level on room air while not in respiratory distress, no cardiac intervention needed at this stage, offer to review) and a closing line of thanks and the start of a sign-off.
